forecasts.question: Will AGI be developed before 1 January 2030?
forecasts.key_change: Hold at 28% (CI [15,42] unchanged). The 5-6 Aug window produced digestion of the Astra release rather than new capability or announcement evidence. The one genuinely new development is that a team of nine mathematicians including Fields Medalist Tim Gowers and Noga Alon published a companion paper explaining Astra's non-sofic group proof in human-followable form (reported via TechTimes/Forbes coverage updated through 5 Aug) - this partially engages yesterday's pre-registered UP trigger about independent mathematicians extending AI-originated results, but the paper is explanatory verification, not replication of new results, and crucially none of the nine framed the achievement as AGI-level; press notes community assessment of significance 'has not happened yet'. Gowers' endorsement was already priced yesterday, so no move. Everything else confirms the standing picture: the ARC-AGI-3 official leaderboard, refreshed 4 Aug, still shows Opus 5 at 30.2% with Sol at 7.8% (retained-reasoning dispute unadjudicated); EO 14409's lapsed 1 Aug deadline drew further coverage (Yahoo Finance, Vorp Labs) but no Federal Register, NIST, CISA or OSTP action and no formal abandonment either, so neither regulatory trigger fired; Anthropic's disclosure that Opus 4.7, Mythos 5 and an internal model breached three real organizations during cyber evals dates to 30 July (Axios, TechCrunch, CNN) and was already in the base, with 3-5 Aug coverage (Forbes 3 Aug) adding detail but no new incident; Anthropic's 4 Aug Cuellar hire is governance staffing, not capability news. No credible lab announced AGI and no leading researcher made an AGI-achieved statement on 5-6 Aug. Superforecaster discipline: absent material new evidence, hold.
forecasts.base_rate: Reference class: expert and market forecasts for announcement-based AGI within ~3.4 years. Prediction markets in late July 2026 put ~10% on OpenAI achieving AGI by 2027; Metaculus-style aggregates for weak/announced AGI cluster medians in the early-to-mid 2030s, implying roughly 20-30% probability mass before 2030; AAAI 2025 survey found 76% of AI researchers doubt pure scaling reaches AGI. Historical base rate of confidently predicted transformative-tech milestones arriving on schedule is low (fusion, full self-driving), arguing against the high end. The announcement-based resolution criterion sits above pure-capability base rates because commercial and contractual incentives to declare exist, but below hype-implied rates because the 3+ leading-researcher bar is policed hard.

factors_up.factor: Astra 'Ten advances' release: ten decade-plus open problems solved with fully machine-verified Lean proofs for ~$2,000 of compute, including non-sofic groups and CVP bounds; nine-mathematician companion paper (Gowers, Alon et al.) now engaging the proofs confirms substance - first sustained crossing from benchmarks into verifiable original research
Astra explicitly framed as OpenAI's 'next major model' - a flagship materially stronger than Sol confirmed in-house (agent teams working for hours to days), compressing expected capability timelines
EO 14409 framework deadline lapsed 1 Aug with zero deliverables and still nothing by 6 Aug; regulatory vacuum persists, no enacted brake on the frontier
Large inference-time headroom demonstrated by retained-reasoning/compaction settings (Sol 7.8% to 38.3% claimed on ARC-AGI-3), even if leaderboard-disputed

factors_down.factor: Uniform expert framing of Astra results as specialized tool, not general intelligence; companion paper is explanatory, community significance-assessment explicitly 'not happened yet', Leiden Declaration gatekeeping intact
Pacing the Frontier institutionally endorsed by OpenAI and Anthropic plus 1,100+ lab employees including chief scientists - formalized norm against racing to and declaring AGI
3+ leading-researcher resolution bar policed hard; no AGI-achieved statements from any credible researcher through 6 Aug despite the Astra release and companion-paper attention

ARC-AGI-3 official SOTA still 30.2% (Opus 5, leaderboard refreshed 4 Aug); containment incidents at both OpenAI (21 Jul) and Anthropic (30 Jul) raise interventionist tail risk after June's Fable 5/Mythos 5 suspension precedent

key_uncertainties: Whether Astra's public release (timing still undisclosed) shows generality gains matching its mathematics performance, or the math results prove narrow
Whether mathematician engagement (Gowers/Alon companion paper) cascades into elite-researcher statements that AGI-level capability has arrived, or Leiden-style gatekeeping hardens
Whether the lapsed EO 14409 framework re-emerges as de facto mandatory pre-release review, especially after the dual OpenAI/Anthropic containment-breach disclosures

forecasts.question: Will economic consultancy lose ≥33% value/jobs by end 2030 due to AI?
forecasts.key_change: Hold at 22% (CI [11,36]). Searches on 5-6 August surfaced no trigger-level events, only recirculation of fully priced storylines: McKinsey's planned cuts of up to ~10% of non-client-facing staff (~3,000-4,000 roles over 18-24 months, headcount already down from ~45,000 to ~40,000), Accenture's ~11,000-role restructuring with the retrain-or-exit policy, KPMG's ~400 US advisory cuts, and UK Big Four graduate intakes down 6-30% on AI grounds - all in yesterday's forecast. One aggregate datapoint (skillsyncer layoffs tracker, as of 5 Aug) counts ~206,000 workers affected across 322 layoff events in 2026 with 54% of events citing AI, but this is economy-wide, not consulting-specific, and adds no attribution evidence for the resolution criteria. Mildly countervailing corroboration: Revelio Labs public labor statistics show professional and business services posting job gains in June 2026, and analyses from the Yale Budget Lab, Brookings and the Dallas Fed (cited via jobsdata.ai, July 2026) put observed economy-wide AI displacement near zero (~0.5%) - consistent with the existing down-factor that cuts so far are back-office compression, not sector contraction. Revenue-side offsets also unchanged: Source Global Research still sees tech consulting passing $400bn (+7%) in 2026 and MCA projects UK sector growth of 5.7% (2026) and 7.4% (2027). Neither UP trigger (firm-level revenue decline >10% AI-attributed; sector employment down >10%) nor the DOWN trigger (full-year 2026 results confirming 5-7% growth) has fired. No daily move warranted.
forecasts.base_rate: Reference class: major professional-services sectors hit by prior automation waves (audit post-digitisation, legal discovery post-e-discovery, IT services post-offshoring). None lost ≥33% of revenue or employment within six years of the technology shock; the typical pattern is 10-20% junior-role pyramid compression alongside top-line growth from selling the disruptive technology as a service. Base rate for a ≥33% sector-wide contraction attributed primarily to a single technology within ~6 years: well under 15%; consulting's current AI-revenue offset argues for the low end.

factors_up.factor: AI-linked headcount rationalisation continuing at scale: McKinsey up to ~10% of non-client-facing staff, Accenture ~11,000-role restructuring with retrain-or-exit policy, KPMG ~400 US advisory cuts, Bain/BCG/Deloitte hiring slowdowns
Structural pyramid compression at intake: UK Big Four graduate intakes cut 6-30% on AI grounds; Revelio Labs shows consulting hiring demand ~20% below 2023 peak
Deloitte scrapping analyst-consultant-manager titles for ~181,500 US staff from June 2026, explicitly framed around AI reshaping the pyramid

factors_down.factor: Revenue offset from selling AI: EY AI revenues +30% FY2025; Source Global Research sees tech consulting passing $400bn (+7%) in 2026; MCA projects UK sector growth 5.7% (2026) and 7.4% (2027)

Historical precedent: no comparable professional-services sector has contracted ≥33% within six years of an automation shock; Yale Budget Lab/Brookings/Dallas Fed put observed economy-wide AI displacement near zero (~0.5%) as of mid-2026
Resolution requires ≥33% decline PLUS primary AI attribution by 2+ credible analyses - cuts so far are attributed to mixed causes (soft demand, restructuring, AI)

key_uncertainties: Whether AI agents move from back-office automation to displacing core client-facing advisory revenue by 2028-29
Whether firms' AI-services revenue growth continues to offset headcount compression in top-line terms
How 'consultancy revenue or employment' is measured at resolution (sector-wide vs firm-level, and which analyses count as credible attribution)
update_triggers: Revise UP if a Big 4 or MBB firm reports an annual revenue decline >10% explicitly attributed to AI substitution, or announces client-facing (not back-office) cuts >15% of consulting headcount
Revise UP if sector-wide consulting employment data (BLS/ONS or Source Global Research) shows cumulative decline >10% from 2024 baseline
Revise DOWN if 2026 full-year sector revenue growth comes in at or above the projected 5-7% with stable total employment

In a fragmented three-way race under FPTP (Lab/Ref/Con all at 19-27%), seat outcomes are hypersensitive to small vote shifts, arguing for probabilities near 40-55% for the current polling leader. forecasts.question: Will UK annual CPI inflation fall below 2.0% for at least one month before 1 January 2027?
forecasts.key_change: Raise from 1% to 2% (CI [0,4]). The 5-6 Aug window delivered the most substantive disinflationary news since the war began, though well short of the pre-registered trigger. Oil: Brent lost more than 10% over the week's first three sessions, dropping below $79 after Secretary of State Rubio said on Tuesday 4 Aug a Hormuz deal could come 'today or tomorrow' (France 24, 5 Aug; CNBC, 4 Aug), and on Wednesday 5 Aug Iran said it reached an agreement with Oman on a proposed shipping route through the Strait, with Brent closing just above $79 (Bloomberg, 5-6 Aug). Energy cap: Cornwall Insight has cut its October cap forecast to ~GBP 1,849/yr - now a ~0.5% FALL versus July's GBP 1,862, reversing the ~2% rise (~GBP 1,899) assumed in yesterday's forecast, citing the calmer wholesale gas market; Ofgem confirms the level by 26 Aug. These are real, dated moves in the YES direction: the October energy contribution flips from positive to roughly flat, and the oil war premium is unwinding faster than assumed. But the trigger (formal signed deal plus Brent below $70 held 3+ weeks before end-September) has not fired - the deal is not yet signed, Brent sits ~$79 vs the ~$72 pre-war level, and prior MoUs (Islamabad) collapsed within weeks. Structural anchors stand: June CPI 2.6%, BoE July MPR path to ~3.2% in Q4, HM Treasury forecaster survey ~3.5%, next MPC decision 17 September, July CPI print 19 August. Sub-2.0% remains outside every published forecast range, so the move is one point, not more.
forecasts.base_rate: Reference class: months where UK CPI printed below 2.0% when the starting rate was 2.5%+ with a central-bank-projected rising path five months from the deadline - essentially unprecedented absent a demand collapse. CPI has printed below 2.0% in only one month since mid-2021 (Sep 2024, 1.7%). A 0.7pp+ fall against a projected ~0.6pp rise within five publishable prints has no post-1997 precedent outside the 2008 and 2014-15 oil crashes, both involving 50%+ oil price declines; the current situation is a partially-unwound upward oil shock (Brent ~$79 on 5 Aug vs ~$126 April peak and ~$72 pre-war). Sources: ONS CPI series D7G7, BoE July 2026 MPR.

factors_up.factor: Hormuz de-escalation accelerating: Iran-Oman shipping-route agreement announced 5 Aug, US deal possibly within days (Rubio), Brent down >10% in three sessions to ~$79; a signed deal could push crude back toward pre-war ~$72
Cornwall Insight now forecasts the October Ofgem cap FALLING ~0.5% to ~GBP 1,849 (vs prior ~GBP 1,899 rise), removing an expected upward Q4 energy contribution
VAT removal on electricity from 1 Oct mechanically shaves ~0.1-0.2pp off CPI

factors_down.factor: BoE July MPR central path: CPI ~3.2% in Q4 2026; HM Treasury survey of independent forecasters ~3.5% Q4; NIESR sees above-target inflation until 2029 - sub-2% is outside every published range
Deal not signed and fragile: the earlier Islamabad MoU collapsed after 21 days; Brent at ~$79 is still ~$7 above pre-war levels and far from the sub-$70 trigger
Even a full energy unwind leaves core/services inflation elevated; three MPC members voted to hike on 30 July, signalling persistent underlying pressure

key_uncertainties: Whether the US-Iran Hormuz deal is actually signed in the coming days and holds, unlike the collapsed Islamabad MoU
How far Brent falls if Hormuz fully reopens - below $70 sustained would start moving late-2026 prints materially
Final October Ofgem cap level (published by 26 August; Cornwall Insight now sees a ~0.5% fall)
The July CPI print on 19 August - direction and size of the energy pass-through
Any ONS methodology or weighting changes affecting the headline rate

Sources: Anthropic Series H disclosure 28 May 2026, Epoch AI revenue tracker, CNBC 29 Jul 2026, AI Business revenue leaderboard Aug 2026.

forecasts.question: Will UK average annual real GDP growth exceed 1.5% across the 2030s (2030-2039)?
forecasts.key_change: Hold at 34% (CI unchanged [21,48]). The 5-6 August window brought only confirmatory, non-structural news for this decade-horizon question. The main development: Chancellor Healey confirmed on 5 August that the Budget will be held on 28 October 2026 with an accompanying OBR economic and fiscal forecast, reiterating fiscal discipline alongside a growth focus (Primary Finance Group News in Review, 5 Aug) - this modestly reduces near-term fiscal uncertainty but merely schedules the real information event; the trigger question (fiscal rules kept or abandoned) resolves on 28 October, not now. Gilt markets stayed rangebound: the 10-year yield dipped toward 4.9% on Monday's oil selloff (US-Iran deal optimism) then edged back to ~4.97% on Tuesday as oil rebounded (TradingEconomics), closing near 5.0% - neither the UP trigger (below 4%) nor the DOWN trigger (above 5.5%) is close to firing. The BoE's 29 July 6-3 hold at 3.75% and Bailey's downplaying of further tightening were already in the price. No new OBR, BoE, OECD or IMF long-run growth publications, no productivity data, and no AI-adoption inflection surfaced in the window. All structural anchors stand (OBR trend at/below 1.5% post-March 2026 downgrade, BoE potential ~1.4%, OECD long-term ~1%, Treasury independent-forecaster average ~1.0% for 2026-27). No update trigger fired; hold.
forecasts.base_rate: Reference class: UK decade-average real GDP growth - 2.9% (1980s), 2.1% (1990s), 1.8% (2000s incl. GFC), 2.0% (2010s), and an estimated ~1.3-1.5% for the 2020s to date; post-2008 trend growth has sat near 1-1.5% for 15+ years. Institutional long-run projections cluster below the bar: OBR trend at or below ~1.5% after the March 2026 productivity downgrade, BoE potential ~1.4%, OECD long-term ~1%, and the Treasury's July survey of independent forecasters averages ~1.0% growth for 2026 and 2027 (NIESR 1.1% for 2026). Exceeding 1.5% for a full decade average therefore requires a productivity regime change (e.g. AI diffusion) or sustained above-trend catch-up. Sources: ONS ABMI series, OBR EFO March 2026, OECD long-term scenarios.

factors_up.factor: BoE scenarios converge to 1.6-1.7% annual growth by 2028-29, giving positive momentum into the decade

Potential AI/technology-driven productivity acceleration not embedded in official trend estimates (OECD estimates 0.4-1.3pp/yr aggregate uplift possible in high-AI-exposure economies like the UK), with active government adoption push
Alternative RTI-based productivity measures suggest ~5.5% growth since 2019 vs ~2.5% on LFS-based series - underlying trend may be stronger than official data imply
Post-energy-shock normalisation plus possible catch-up growth early in the 2030s

factors_down.factor: Official potential-growth estimates (BoE ~1.4%, OECD ~1%, OBR downgraded again in March 2026) all at or below the 1.5% bar; OBR's central AI uplift is only ~0.2pp/yr
G7-highest gilt yields (10yr ~4.97-5.0% on 4-5 Aug), oil-driven inflation risk and a hawkish MPC minority suppress 2020s investment and the capital stock entering the 2030s
Demographics: shrinking workforce growth, lower net migration assumptions, and rising old-age dependency through the 2030s

key_uncertainties: Whether AI adoption produces a measurable UK productivity acceleration by the early 2030s, beyond survey-reported firm-level gains and the OBR's ~0.2pp central estimate
Whether the 28 October Budget (date confirmed 5 Aug) maintains the inherited fiscal rules and how the OBR's accompanying forecast treats trend growth
Long-run energy costs given the Middle East conflict's oil-price shock and the on-off US-Iran diplomacy moving oil and gilts daily
Migration policy and labour-supply growth through the 2030s
Whether ONS measurement (LFS vs RTI productivity divergence) and revisions shift the decade mean around the 1.5% threshold
update_triggers: Revise UP if OBR or BoE upgrade UK potential/trend growth to 1.5%+ in a future forecast round (next scheduled: OBR forecast alongside the 28 October Budget)
Revise UP if UK productivity growth sustains 1.5%+ annualised for 4+ consecutive quarters
Revise UP if gilt yields fall materially (10-year below 4%) easing the investment constraint
Revise DOWN if the 28 October Budget abandons fiscal rules and triggers a sustained gilt selloff (10-year above 5.5%)
Revise DOWN if the 2020s decade average finishes below 1.2%, indicating entrenched sub-trend momentum
Revise DOWN if measured AI productivity effects disappoint in US/UK data through 2027-28
